security.metaDescription: Learn how TextSafe encrypts messages, what it protects, and its limitations.
security.title: Security at TextSafe
security.intro: TextSafe is designed so the service does not need your plaintext or password.

sections.title: Encryption in your browser
sections.body: Your device derives a 256-bit key from the password with PBKDF2-SHA-256 and a random salt, then encrypts the message with AES-256-GCM and a unique 12-byte IV. Only the resulting ciphertext is sent to the server.

sections.title: Passwords cannot be recovered
sections.body: Passwords are never sent to or stored by TextSafe. If a password is lost, neither TextSafe nor the database administrator can recover the message.

sections.title: Salt and IV
sections.body: The random salt and IV are not secrets. They are stored with the ciphertext and must be unique for safe key derivation and authenticated encryption.

sections.title: Burn after reading
sections.body: The server considers a message read when its ciphertext is first retrieved. It cannot know whether decryption succeeded, so a wrong password can permanently consume a burn-after-reading message.

sections.title: Minimum metadata
sections.body: The application stores expiration and delivery settings. Hosting infrastructure may still process technical metadata such as IP address, request time, and user agent in access logs.

sections.title: Protect your device
sections.body: Malware, keyloggers, malicious browser extensions, screenshots, clipboard managers, phishing, or a compromised device can expose a message before or after encryption.

security.separateBody: Send the secret link and password through different trusted channels. Anyone who obtains both can decrypt the message.
protects: A database leak containing only ciphertext
A database administrator trying to read message contents
Accidental plaintext storage by this application
Undetected ciphertext modification, through AES-GCM authentication
notProtects: Sending the link and password together
Someone who already knows the password
security.critical: Do not use TextSafe as the only protection for emergencies or extremely critical data. No web application can guarantee the security of a compromised device.

faq.metaDescription: Answers about TextSafe encryption, storage, passwords, expiration, and privacy.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Straightforward answers about how encrypted messages work.

items.a: TextSafe is designed not to receive the plaintext or password. Encryption and decryption happen in your browser.
Supabase stores an encrypted payload containing ciphertext, salt, IV, and key-derivation parameters, plus delivery settings.
No. The password stays in browser memory only while you use the form and is never sent to the API.

items.q: What happens if I forget my password?
items.a: The message cannot be recovered. There is no password reset or recovery key.

items.q: What does burn after reading mean?
items.a: The encrypted payload can be retrieved once. It is consumed at retrieval time, even if the recipient later enters a wrong password.

items.q: Why should I send the password separately?
items.a: Separating the link and password reduces the chance that one intercepted conversation exposes both parts.

items.q: Can an expired message be recovered?
items.a: No. Expired records are rejected and removed.
No absolute anonymity is promised. Hosting providers may process IP addresses and user agents in infrastructure logs.
AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption with keys derived using PBKDF2-SHA-256, a random salt, and 600,000 iterations.

items.q: Is TextSafe a replacement for an encrypted messenger?
items.a: No. It is a small tool for sharing an encrypted note, not a complete end-to-end encrypted conversation platform.

privacy.metaDescription: Understand what TextSafe stores and what hosting infrastructure may process.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: TextSafe minimizes the data needed to provide expiring encrypted messages.

sections.title: No account required
sections.body: You do not create an account or profile to create or open a message.

sections.title: Message storage
sections.body: TextSafe does not intentionally store plaintext or passwords. It stores ciphertext, salt, IV, key-derivation parameters, expiration time, and burn-after-reading settings.

sections.title: Retention
sections.body: Records remain until their expiration time, or are consumed earlier when burn after reading is enabled. Cleanup jobs remove expired records.

sections.title: Technical metadata
sections.body: Vercel, Supabase, network providers, and other hosting infrastructure may process IP addresses, request times, user agents, and operational logs. TextSafe therefore does not claim zero logs.

sections.title: Analytics and advertising
sections.body: Analytics and third-party scripts are not loaded on secret-message pages. TextSafe does not sell or use message contents for advertising.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.intro: Use TextSafe responsibly and understand its limits.
items: You are responsible for the content you create and share.
Do not use TextSafe for illegal activity.

Burn-after-reading messages cannot be recovered after retrieval.
